item.title: AWS Enhances API and AI Endpoint Security
item.description:
AWS Enhances API and AI Endpoint Security

AWS has launched new capabilities to discover and protect APIs and AI endpoints, addressing the evolving landscape of digital business and AI agent interactions.

🔍 Overview

  • AWS has introduced new features to help discover and protect APIs and AI endpoints.
  • This includes API Portal in Amazon API Gateway, API Security, and AI Security managed rule groups in AWS WAF.

🧩 How it works

  • API Portal discovers APIs and AI endpoints from configuration and live traffic.
  • API Security protects against broken object level authorization, authentication attacks, and reconnaissance.
  • AI Security identifies AI traffic, validates requests, and checks prompts and responses through Amazon Bedrock Guardrails.

⚙️ Key details

  • API Portal is available in the Amazon API Gateway console.
  • API Security and AI Security are available in the AWS WAF console.
  • The new features work with Amazon CloudFront, Amazon API Gateway REST APIs, and Application Load Balancer.

🚀 Availability

  • API Portal, API Security, and AI Security are generally available today.

💡 Why it matters

  • APIs have run digital businesses for over a decade.
  • In 2026, AI endpoints joined them, leading to a need for new security measures.
  • AI agents now act on behalf of users, requiring robust protection of APIs and AI endpoints.

#AWS #APISecurity #AIEndpoints #CloudSecurity #DigitalBusiness

Source: Introducing API and AI security on AWS, from discovery to protection | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Kong Gateway introduces AI traffic capabilities and MCP governance
item.description:
Kong Gateway introduces AI traffic capabilities and MCP governance

Kong or Kong Gateway is a cloud-native, platform-agnostic, scalable API, LLM, and MCP Gateway distinguished for its high performance and extensibility via plugins. It provides advanced AI traffic capabilities with multi-LLM support, semantic security, MCP traffic security and analytics, and more.

🔍 Overview

Kong serves as the central layer for orchestrating microservices or conventional API traffic - and agentic LLM and MCP as well - with ease. By providing functionality for proxying, routing, load balancing, health checking, and authentication, it manages traffic across various architectures.

⚙️ Key details

  • Universal LLM API: Routes traffic across multiple providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, GCP Gemini, AWS Bedrock, Azure AI, Databricks, Mistral, and Huggingface.
  • MCP Capabilities: Includes MCP traffic governance, security, observability, and autogeneration from any RESTful API.
  • AI Features: Offers over 60 features such as AI observability, semantic security, caching, and semantic routing.
  • Security and Routing: Supports authentication and authorization via JWT, basic auth, OAuth, and ACLs.
  • Traffic Management: Handles proxying, SSL/TLS termination, and connectivity support for L4 or L7 traffic.
  • Plugins: Includes 60+ plugins for traffic controls, rate limiting, request/response transformations, logging, and monitoring.
Feature Description
Advanced Routing Load balancing and health checking configurable via RESTful admin API or declarative configuration
Deployment Models Supports Declarative Databaseless Deployment and Hybrid Deployment with control plane/data plane separation
Kubernetes Support Runs natively on Kubernetes thanks to its official Kubernetes Ingress Controller
Plugin Hub Showcases Kong Inc. and community-developed plugins like AWS Lambda, Correlation ID, and Response Transformer

🚀 Availability

Kong is available in various distributions depending on the deployment environment. Users can run it in the cloud, on bare metal, or using containers.

  • Cloud: Sign up for a free trial of Kong Konnect to get started with a cloud-hosted solution.
  • Docker: The docker-compose distribution is suggested for easy setup. A docker installation procedure is also available for running the Kong Gateway in DB-less mode.
  • Installation: To start with the Docker distribution, clone the Docker repository and navigate to the compose folder. Use the command $ KONG_DATABASE=postgres docker-compose --profile database up to start the Gateway stack.

Once started, the Gateway is available on localhost with the following ports:

  • 8000: Send traffic to your service via Kong.
  • 8001: Configure Kong using Admin API or via decK.
  • 8002: Access Kong’s management Web UI (Kong Manager).

#Kong #APIGateway #MCP #LLM #Kubernetes #DevOps

Source: Kong/kong

item.title: Azure AI Gateway launched with security, cost control, and extensibility features
item.description:
Azure AI Gateway launched with security, cost control, and extensibility features

Microsoft has launched the AI Gateway, powered by Azure API Management, offering tools for securing, optimizing, and extending AI model deployments. The service provides multiple capabilities for managing AI workflows.

🔍 Overview

The AI Gateway delivers core functionalities across five key areas: security, performance, observability, cost control, and extensibility. It includes features like OAuth 2.0 authentication, load balancing, semantic caching, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) support.

🧩 Key Features

Core capabilities include:

  • Security: OAuth 2.0, managed identities, content safety filtering
  • Performance: Load balancing, semantic caching, request routing
  • Observability: Token metrics, built-in logging, tracing
  • Cost Control: Rate limiting, quota management, FinOps framework
  • Extensibility: MCP protocol support, function calling, multi-model routing

🛠️ Technical Components

Specific technical implementations include:

Component Description
Backend Pool Load Balancing Distribute requests across multiple model endpoints
Token Rate Limiting Control token consumption via rate limiting policies
Semantic Caching Cache responses using vector similarity for faster/cheaper completions
Model Routing Route requests to different backends based on model/version
FinOps Framework Manage AI budgets through automated quota controls
Model Context Protocol (MCP) Plug-and-play tools with OAuth credential management

🧪 Hands-On Labs

Over 30 hands-on labs are available at aka.ms/ai-gateway/labs. Each lab provides:

  • Step-by-step Jupyter notebooks
  • Bicep infrastructure templates
  • APIM policies for Azure deployment

🚀 Availability

The AI Gateway Dev Portal is now live. Prerequisites for use include:

  • Python 3.12+
  • uv (fast Python package manager)
  • VS Code with Jupyter extension
  • Azure subscription with Contributor + RBAC Administrator roles
  • Azure CLI authenticated to your subscription

🌐 Integration Examples

Supported integrations include:

  • OpenAI function calling with Azure Functions backend
  • Realtime audio APIs combined with MCP tools
  • Google Gemini models via MCP
  • A2A-enabled agents with plug-and-play tools

#Azure #AIGateway #APIManagement #AIAgents #MCP #FinOps

Source: Azure-Samples/AI-Gateway

item.title: Codex Pooler Introduced as Self-Hosted Gateway for Codex-Compatible Agents
item.description:
Codex Pooler Introduced as Self-Hosted Gateway for Codex-Compatible Agents

Codex Pooler is a self-hosted gateway designed to run Codex-compatible agents, tools, and automation using stable Pool API keys.

🔍 Overview

Codex Pooler allows operators to manage pools, accounts, API keys, saved resets, routing, request accounting, audit logs, and health. The system is designed so that operators do not store raw Codex secrets, bearer tokens, prompts, files, audio, or images.

🧩 How it works

Clients send OpenAI-compatible or Codex backend requests to the Codex Pooler. The system then selects an eligible account based on the following criteria:

  • Model support
  • Quota evidence
  • Limits
  • Session continuity
  • Routing policy
  • Health

⚙️ Key details

Feature Description
Stable Pool API keys Provides clients with one credential regardless of whether the Pool has one or several upstream accounts, avoiding the distribution of raw Codex account material.
Eligibility-aware routing Routes requests to accounts with matching health, session state, Pool policy, usable quota evidence, and compatible model support.
Codex backend compatibility Allows Codex-compatible clients to point at Codex Pooler while maintaining usage, compacting, and responses.

💡 Why it matters

  • Credential Isolation: It works with one upstream Codex account for client normalization, metadata-only operations, saved reset visibility, and credential isolation.
  • Scalability: Additional accounts can be added for routing and shared capacity across eligible accounts.
  • Stability: The Pool key remains stable even when capacity, reset policy, lifecycle state, and upstream assignments change.
  • Administrative Control: Instance owners maintain the global administration surface, while instance admins are restricted to their assigned Pools.

#Codex #API #AIagents #SelfHosted

Source: icoretech/codex-pooler

item.title: OpenRouter Model Routing and Provider Control Features
item.description:
OpenRouter Model Routing and Provider Control Features

OpenRouter provides an API endpoint that automatically handles fallbacks and selects the most cost-effective option for model requests.

⚙️ Key details

Because different providers use various serving software, optimizations, and settings, the same OpenRouter endpoint can result in requests that behave in different ways. These differences include:

  • Some providers lack vision capability for vision models.
  • The processing of the reasoning effort option can differ between providers.

🧩 How it works

Users have tools to manage how their requests are routed:

  • provider.only option: Allows users to control which specific provider is routed to.
  • /endpoints method: Returns a list of available providers for a specific model ID.

#OpenRouter #API #LLM #ModelRouting

Source: So you want to use OpenRouter?
